title: 2024 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement:
On top of a rectangular card with sides of length \(1\) and \(2+\sqrt3,\) an identical card is placed so that two of their diagonals line up, as shown (\(AC,\) in this case).

Continue the process, adding a third card to the second, and so on, lining up successive diagonals after rotating clockwise. In total, how many cards must be used until a vertex of a new card lands exactly on the vertex labeled \(B\) in the figure?

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: No new vertex will land on \(B.\)

solutions.text:
A diagonal makes an angle \(\theta\) with a long side, where \(\tan\theta=\dfrac{1}{2+\sqrt3}\) \(=2-\sqrt3=\tan15^\circ.\) Thus the acute angle between the two diagonals of a card is \(2\theta=30^\circ.\)

Each new card shares one diagonal with the previous card, and its other diagonal is the next line obtained by turning \(30^\circ\) clockwise. All these equal diagonals have the same midpoint and are diameters of one common circle. The line through the original card’s other diagonal, which contains \(B,\) is \(30^\circ\) counterclockwise from \(AC.\) As an unoriented line, this is the same as \(150^\circ\) clockwise from \(AC.\) Five additions advance the unused diagonal by \(5\cdot30^\circ=150^\circ,\) so the sixth card is the first new card with a vertex at \(B.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The diagonal makes angle \(\arctan\dfrac{1}{2+\sqrt3}=15^\circ\) with the long side, since \(\dfrac{1}{2+\sqrt3}=2-\sqrt3\)
The two diagonals meet at \(30^\circ;\) track the unused diagonal as five new cards are added
